news_summary: Nebius Group (NBIS) reported Q2 2026 results on Aug 12, 2026: revenue of $582.3M and EPS of -$0.12, alongside $236M of positive adjusted EBITDA; management raised 2026 capex guidance to $20-25B (from $16-20B) and reiterated full-year targets of $7-9B ARR, $3-3.4B group revenue, and roughly 40% adjusted EBITDA margin, citing more than 3.5GW of contracted power and a target of at least 4GW by year-end. The company continues building out its AI-cloud/inference stack: it achieved NVIDIA 'Exemplar Cloud' validation on GB300 NVL72 for training in April 2026 alongside a $2B NVIDIA strategic investment, and closed the Clarifai team/IP licensing deal on May 12, 2026 following the earlier Tavily and Eigen AI acquisitions, aimed at building a vertically integrated 'Token Factory' inference platform. Nebius is also advancing a second U.S. gigawatt-scale site: a 1.2GW AI-factory campus at Highridge Business Park in Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania (roughly 600 acres, phased from 260MW in October 2027 toward 1GW+ by late 2029), alongside its existing Missouri campus. The next earnings call is scheduled for around Nov 10, 2026.

catalysts.what: Nebius reported Q2 2026 revenue of $582.3M and EPS of -$0.12, with $236M of positive adjusted EBITDA; raised FY2026 capex guidance to $20-25B and reiterated ARR target of $7-9B, group revenue of $3-3.4B, and roughly 40% adjusted EBITDA margin.

Nebius achieved NVIDIA 'Exemplar Cloud' status on NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 for training workloads (meeting the 95% performance threshold across NVIDIA's reference benchmarking recipes), part of a broader relationship that includes a $2B strategic investment from NVIDIA.

Nebius brought in Clarifai's core engineering/research team (led by founder/CEO Matthew Zeiler, joining as SVP of Research) and licensed Clarifai's inference and compute-orchestration technology and patents on a non-exclusive, perpetual basis (excludes legacy computer-vision and government/defense IP); financial terms were not disclosed.

Nebius detailed a 1.2GW, roughly 600-acre AI-factory data center campus at Highridge Business Park, Butler Township, Schuylkill County, PA (its second U.S. gigawatt-scale site after Missouri), with an initial 260MW phase targeted for October 2027 and full buildout (1GW+) by late 2029; a community open house was held Aug 6, 2026.
Nebius acquired Eigen AI, recognized by NVIDIA as a top speed-inference provider, for approximately $643M, adding model-level inference optimization to its Token Factory stack.

move_thesis: NBIS's re-rating is being driven by demonstrated hyperscale AI-infrastructure execution -- triple-digit revenue growth, NVIDIA GB300 performance validation, a second U.S. gigawatt-scale campus in Pennsylvania, and a string of inference-stack acquisitions (Tavily, Eigen AI, Clarifai) -- set against a sharply higher capex plan ($20-25B for 2026) that raises funding and execution risk. The next checkpoints are delivery against the raised ARR/EBITDA targets and the Q3 call expected around Nov 10, 2026.
